column3: “From his morsel” is rendered “of his bread”; NASB prints the parable as poetry.
“He spared to take” is rendered “he was unwilling to take,” and “sheep … cattle” as “flock … herd.”
“A son of death” is rendered “deserves to die.”
NASB adds “It is I who” for the emphatic pronouns.
“Into your bosom” is rendered “into your care,” and “like those and like those” as “many more things like these.”
The Hebrew reads “in My eyes”; NASB has “in His sight.”
“Calamity” is rendered “evil,” “neighbor” as “companion,” and “to the eyes of this sun” as “in broad daylight.”
The Hebrew reads “you have utterly despised the enemies of the LORD,” often taken as a scribal softening; NASB renders “given occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme.”
“The wife of Uriah” is rendered “Uriah’s widow,” and NASB adds “very.”
NASB supplies “all night” and does not have “in sackcloth.”
“She called his name” (written text) is rendered “he named him,” following the spoken reading.
NASB supplies “word,” and joins the verse to verse 24.
“My name will be called on it” is rendered “it will be named after me.”
NASB supplies “in it was” for the precious stone; “their king” may also be read as the god “Milcom.”
